identity.name: Sodium acetates (sodium acetate and sodium hydrogen diacetate)
identity.chemical_class: Salts and acid salts of acetic acid (short-chain carboxylate food additives)

function.mechanism: Acidification and buffering effects plus antimicrobial activity associated with acetate/acetic acid systems.

adi.basis: EFSA (2022) cites prior EFSA conclusion (2013) that establishing an ADI for acetic acid/acetates is not considered necessary.

efsa.key_finding: E262 is already authorised in the EU; EFSA re-evaluation entries are ongoing, and a related 2022 EFSA opinion on acetate-based buffered vinegar found no safety concern at proposed use levels (but not at quantum satis).

adi.basis: JECFA lists sodium acetate (INS 262(i)) as ADI not limited and sodium hydrogen diacetate (INS 262(ii)) as ADI 0-15 mg/kg bw (both evaluation year 1973; sodium acetate note indicates maintenance at 49th meeting, 1997).

concerns.summary: Recent in vitro studies in human lymphocytes/cell models reported concentration-dependent DNA damage, chromosomal aberrations, or cytotoxic effects at higher sodium acetate/sodium diacetate concentrations.
Some non-human cell/microalgae systems show condition-dependent toxicity for sodium diacetate (greater under acidic conditions), with limited direct relevance to normal dietary human exposure.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2022 concluded no safety concern at proposed maximum/typical use levels for buffered vinegar (acetate-based).
FDA lists sodium acetate and sodium diacetate as GRAS-affirmed direct food ingredients under specified conditions.
JECFA sodium acetate record uses ADI 'not limited' with maintenance note at 49th meeting.

adi_exceedance.notes: No direct ADI exceedance determination was identified for E262 in reviewed sources. EFSA reports high-end modeled exposure for buffered vinegar in young children but still concluded no safety concern at proposed levels; sodium-sensitive individuals remain a general dietary-sodium consideration.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory bodies (EFSA/FDA/JECFA) broadly support safety under defined use conditions, while recent adverse findings are mainly high-concentration in vitro signals without strong corroborating epidemiological or in vivo dietary harm evidence at typical exposure levels.
key_factors: EFSA/FDA/JECFA permissive regulatory status with conditions
EFSA ADI-not-necessary framing for acetate context
JECFA split ADI outputs between 262(i) and 262(ii)
In vitro genotoxicity/cytotoxicity signals at high concentrations
No IARC group listing identified for sodium acetate/diacetate
